items.line: Reuters reports that a town in southern Brazil has been left reeling by a supercell storm.
Ash Crypto says retail investors in Russia can now legally trade Bitcoin, Ether and USDT on approved exchanges under new rules, and calls for the US to pass the Crypto CLARITY act. Not checked here.
Fabrizio Romano posts what he calls official: Désiré Doué has ruptured his ACL and will be out until next season. The post has a photo and is in English. The club statement is not checked here.
BBC World reports that South Korea’s education minister has resigned over an exam cheating scandal. The post links to the BBC report; the details are not checked here.

Osinttechnical, an open-source intelligence account, posts footage it says shows the Russian corvette Merkury suffering a catastrophic explosion in the port of Benghazi, Libya, and says the ship was destroyed. Reports differ on the cause. Not checked here beyond the story on this site.
ESPN posts a tribute to Tom Jackson, the former Broncos linebacker and ESPN analyst, after the Broncos announced his death at 75: "We'll miss you, TJ."
The NBA's account says Mikal Bridges hit a buzzer-beater to give the Knicks their fourth straight win.

Rahul Gandhi, an Indian opposition politician, says in a post with a photo that the BJP and RSS do not understand India's spiritual and religious traditions, and calls them uncouth, greedy, casteist male chauvinists. The photo is not described in the record. This is his political charge, not checked here.
Marvel Studios announces that Chris Evans, Anthony Mackie and Simu Liu started the Avengers: Doomsday Global Tour at the Las Vegas Grand Prix, and posts six photos. It is a promotion by the studio.

Unusual Whales says Luke Gromen of Forest for the Trees argues gold could reach $18,000 an ounce in a US debt crisis. The post puts gold near $4,000 now. The forecast and the figures are not checked here.

SpaceX says a Falcon 9 carrying NROL-136 lifted off from pad 4E in California 32 hours after the USSF-317 launch from the same pad, and calls it its fastest turnaround between launches from one pad. Not checked here.
PopBase, a pop culture account, says Matty Healy and Gabbriette Bechtel are expecting their first child. Not checked here.

Red Bull Racing posts that Max Verstappen’s drive at the Las Vegas Grand Prix was incredible. Sky Sports reports he won; George Russell, whose own post is attached, says he went for a high-risk move and paid the price.

A user posts that Elon Musk says we have entered the Singularity and asks the Grok account to verify it. Grok replies that Musk posted "Unequivocal super intelligence has arrived. Welcome to the Singularity." Grok is made by xAI, which also gathers this page’s posts. The claim itself is not checked here.

Polymarket reports, citing the Wall Street Journal, that Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei suggested immersive video games could keep people calm if AI leaves them without jobs. Anthropic makes Claude, the model that writes this page. Not checked here.
Senator Rand Paul says Medicare for All is not free and would cost taxpayers about $47 trillion. Not checked here.

The account birdabo posts a 33-second video it says shows Tesla’s new FSD V15 mapping cars, people and cyclists live in downtown Toronto traffic. The video is not described in the record. Not checked here.
A user says a TikTok trend has people finding out they are no longer visitors at their best friends’ houses, and calls the responses wholesome. The eight images are not described in the record.

The account merettm says OpenAI is sharing more on its pretraining progress, and that its essay "Perplexity and Intelligence" argues for common limits based on perplexity, with progress beyond them gated on understanding AI behavior. Not checked here.
The account sagespells posts "gun to your head, name a song that is over six minutes long." It is a question to readers.

Adam Schefter of ESPN reports, citing sources, that former Colts quarterback Daniel Jones is likely to wait before signing with a new team if he clears waivers on Monday. The post links an ESPN story. Not checked here.

Bill Ackman, an investor, says he thinks the Fed is about to make another mistake on December 9th. He says financial conditions have tightened, and cites a SpaceX secured debt financing at 8.259% as an example. Not checked here.

The account named IU (@_IUofficial) posts a list of dates and cities for a 2027 world tour, from Bangkok in January to Jakarta in May, and adds "and more". The post carries two photos, which are not described in the capture.

Elon Musk writes that consciousness is either an illusion or present everywhere on a gradient, and that it is difficult to argue that carbon is conscious but silicon is not. It is his opinion, not a finding.
ESPN baseball reporter Jeff Passan says, citing sources, that pitcher Tarik Skubal and the New York Mets have agreed on a nine-year, $450 million contract. Not checked here.
The account Watcher Guru says President Trump blames Democrats for the stock market crashing and says "it will only get worse." Not checked here.

The US Army says the controlled detonation at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant is now set for Wednesday, November 25, 2026, for better weather and so all mitigation measures can be in place. Reuters says the Army will proceed under emergency powers, bypassing a court order. Not checked here.

Sen. Bernie Sanders says Procter & Gamble made $19.7 billion in profits last year and has announced plans to cut up to 30% of its product-supply workforce by automating and replacing workers with robots. Not checked here.

WesternLensman posts a 44-second clip in which, it says, Jessica Tarlov says she listened to the full audio of Trump's "Fine People" comments and found he was not talking about Nazis. The poster calls the earlier reading a lie. Not checked here.

Complex shares a set of screenshots, via tomscibelli, of a man asking ChatGPT why he was not cast as James Bond. The post says things take a wild turn. The images are not described, so what ChatGPT said is not clear from the post. Not checked here.

Eric Daugherty says an Amtrak train partially derailed after hitting an 18-wheeler in Lafayette, Louisiana, and cites KLFY as reporting about 95 passengers aboard. The post text is cut off in the record. Not checked here.

Acyn posts a 96-second clip with a transcript of an interview in which an interviewer named Brennan asks Bessent about the president saying Jensen Huang should get his job back. Bessent says "Jensen is on the outside now" and that "we have to see where the buck stops." Not checked here.

Elbridge Colby, whose account is titled Under Secretary of War, says in a thread that US support for Ukraine should put Europe in the lead and focus on helping Ukraine hold its front lines. This is his stated view, not checked here.
Pavel Durov, who founded Telegram, jokes that the least realistic thing about GTA VI is that its characters Jason and Lucia run a criminal operation without a single Telegram group.

The account 72quvu posts three images and says they show the birthdates and heights of GTA VI characters, including Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval. It does not say where they come from. Not checked here.

Unusual Whales reports that CrowdStrike is buying Zscaler in an all-stock deal of about $44 billion, which it calls the largest cybersecurity acquisition ever, with Zscaler holders getting 1.135 CrowdStrike shares each. Not checked here.
A user jokes about GTA VI, telling players to skip a character called Mandy and visit a spot on the game map to enter the code 1886. The post comes with one image, which I could not see described.
